title: Data Placement and Replica Selection for Improving Co-location in Distributed Environments
review_status: full-text audit complete; energy derived from a server power model and system counters, with query-span, latency, load-balance, and workload-trace caveats

venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2013-02-18; full arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: Energy in the motivating experiments is estimated, not directly metered: Mantis-derived Itanium power model uses dstat CPU, network, I/O, and memory counters. Estimated energy rises with span/parallelism in the reported tests, but MySQL TPC-H runtimes also increase (authors suggest a nested-loop join implementation issue), while the custom query processor runtime stays roughly constant. Lower span can increase latency/load imbalance and relies on representative captured workloads.

title: On the limitations of analysing worst-case dynamic energy of processing
review_status: full-text audit complete; formal inapproximability for safe tight worst-case operand-dependent dynamic energy, distinct from mean-energy measurement
sections_checked: average per-instruction energy and safety distinction
operand-dependent processor switching case study
NP-hardness reduction for exact worst-case switching
inapproximability and safe-bound implications
hardware and system-level scope limitations
venue_year_verified: arXiv v4 full text audited; author version identifies 2018 journal publication (ACM TECS, DOI 10.1145/3173042).
evidence_note: Proves exact worst-case operand-switching energy is NP-hard and rules out useful constant/polynomial approximation with guaranteed safety under the formal model. Average random-operand instruction costs are not safe upper bounds. Scope is operand-dependent dynamic processor energy; caches, memory, displays, peripherals, and full-system energy are distinct contributors. This does not imply that average workload energy cannot be measured.

review_status: full-text audit complete; energy savings calculated from assumed component wattage times runtime, with emulated CSD and omitted external-storage transfer time

20-seed experimental protocol

objective and deployment-scope caveats
venue_year_verified: arXiv v2 dated 2026-01-29; initial arXiv submission 2024-04-17; full arXiv v2 PDF audited.
evidence_note: Calculates energy as component processor power times time, assuming 200 W for 40 host CPU threads, 5 W per main process, 85 W for 16 additional processes, and 0.25 W CSD; results average 20 seeds. CSD-only uses less calculated energy but substantially more learning time. CSD is emulated with Pynq, and time for transfer between its external storage and host storage is explicitly ignored; not a whole-system direct meter result.

venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2026-04-28; full arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: Table II reports 142.73–575.12 Wh across nine whole-experiment model/aggregator configurations on a single RTX 6000 Ada setup; lowest energy, best accuracy, and fastest settings differ. The full text calls the environment simulated FL and says energy is logged/system-level, but does not specify meter/counter, calculation procedure, included components, idle treatment, or repeat variance sufficiently to reconstruct Wh from the paper. This is a reproducibility limit, not evidence the values are incorrect; balanced i.i.d. virtual clients do not measure a geographically distributed deployment.
